sources.excerpt: Ripple issuer transparency dashboard, data as of 2026-11-05: RLUSD circulating supply $2,632.9M; reserve funds $2,748.0M. Issuer identified as Standard Custody & Trust Company, LLC. Dashboard says monthly independent CPA reserve attestations are published. The visible September report link resolved to the same August 2026 signed PDF as the August link; no September attestation was verified in this run. Nov 5 balances are issuer-dashboard values, not independently attested by the latest linked report.

Standard Custody & Trust Company, LLC August 2026 RLUSD Reserve Report; independent accountant's opinion dated 2026-09-29; report dates 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-31 at 5:00pm ET. As of Aug 31: outstanding stablecoin units 2,325,969,308; reserve market value $2,446,312,864. The report states reserve assets were equal to or greater than outstanding units and segregated from issuer proprietary assets; eligible assets include short-maturity U.S. Treasuries, qualifying overnight reverse repos, government money-market funds and regulated bank deposits. Both the August and visible September dashboard links resolved to this same August report in this run.

XRPL Dashboard /rlusd page observed 2026-11-08T11:02:40Z; snapshot refreshed 223 seconds before capture; live feed unavailable. Displayed total RLUSD supply $2.68B, Ethereum $1.80B (67.2%), XRPL $878.32M (32.8%); 24h net supply change +$4M overall, Ethereum +$10M mints and no burns, XRPL -$6M net. Dashboard says XRPL data comes from its own node using gateway_balances with public-node fallback; Ethereum uses public RPC and is not anchored in the signed daily snapshot. Displayed total exceeds issuer dashboard Nov5 circulation $2.6329B by about $47.1M (1.79%); do not reconcile or average without common cutoff and chain-by-chain supply proof.

XRPL Dashboard signed snapshot file dated 2026-11-07: rlusd_xrpl_supply 884,538,229.79; leaf hash 4d7dc0c81c2a28b01f49eb8db716b0e3f3aa92b58442c12f09877213ec6830a8; chain root 2ec03309ff1e4ff0fec5629de628fca981971910cff4497cdd2c003d07fd596c; leaf_index 173; leaves_total 174; errors empty. Signature and Merkle inclusion were not cryptographically verified in this run; metric-specific as-of timestamp is not supplied.

Coinbase 2026 Q3 Form 10-Q: stablecoin revenue $306.905M for the three months ended 2026-09-30 versus $324.534M in Q3 2025; nine-month stablecoin revenue $904.487M. The filing says stablecoin revenue rose $84.6M from higher average USDC balances held in Coinbase products and fell $52.8M due to lower average interest rates; revenue on corporate payment-stablecoin balances is presented in Corporate interest and other income rather than Stablecoin revenue. At 2026-09-30, USDC assets on Coinbase platform were $8.616B; total assets on platform $376.645B.

Coinbase Q3 2026 SEC-filed earnings deck: average USDC held in Coinbase products $22B; portion in corporate balances $2B; off-platform USDC $51B; average total USDC market capitalization $73B. The deck's combined Stablecoin Revenue & Revenue on Corporate Balances was $328M: $202M from USDC held in Coinbase products, $21M from corporate balances, and $126M from off-platform USDC. This $328M combined deck measure is not identical to the 10-Q's $306.905M Stablecoin revenue line because corporate-balance revenue is presented separately in the 10-Q.

Circle Q3 2026 Form 10-Q: USDC in circulation end-of-period $73.879B and average $73.264B; Q3 onchain transaction volume $13.9T (+49% YoY); Q3 total revenue and reserve income $865M; reserve return rate 3.5%. Circle states reserve income was 76.0% of Q3 total revenue. Circle incurred $331.3M of distribution costs in connection with Coinbase agreements in Q3 and $986.6M for the first nine months. Circle says Coinbase allocations depend on USDC held on its platform after issuer retention plus a share of remaining ecosystem growth payments after approved third-party participants. This is Circle's contractual distribution cost, not a direct one-for-one comparison with Coinbase's stablecoin revenue.

Circle's transparency page was observed during the 2026-11-08 run and displays a data-as-of date of 2026-11-05, but the browser text extraction did not expose numeric USDC circulation or reserve balances. No Nov 5 USDC circulation value is admitted from this page. Circle's Q3 2026 SEC filing provides end-of-quarter circulation $73.879B and average circulation $73.264B as of 2026-09-30.

SBI Holdings' official 2025 disclosure says SBI Group invested in Ripple in 2016 and held approximately 9% of its shares as largest external shareholder at the June 2025 disclosure date; current November 2026 percentage was not verified. SBI Ripple Asia is a Ripple/SBI joint venture. SBI says SBI Remit began Japan's first international remittance service utilizing XRP in 2021. No current SBI Remit XRP transaction volume was disclosed in the reviewed source.

SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank invested a combined $50M in Circle at its June 2025 IPO ($25M each). SBI says it signed a basic agreement with Circle in November 2023, SBI VC Trade launched USDC for Japanese retail customers in March 2025, and SBI/Circle contracted to establish SBI Circle Holdings as a joint venture. These are USDC relationships distinct from Ripple/RLUSD and JPYSC.

SBI VC Trade's official 2026-06-24 release confirms RLUSD handling in VCTRADE, free deposits and withdrawals, and identifies Standard Custody & Trust Company, LLC (a Ripple subsidiary) as issuer; the official release does not state a supported chain. Contemporaneous secondary reports from CoinPost and Protos say the Japanese VCTRADE product accepted only Ethereum ERC-20 RLUSD, not XRPL RLUSD, at launch. Treat Ethereum-only as secondary-corroborated and do not count this as verified XRPL distribution.

SBI's official 2026-06-24 JPYSC launch notice says SBI Shinsei Trust Bank is issuer, SBI VC Trade handles distribution, and Startale Group is joint developer and SBI equity-method affiliate. Initial availability is limited to SBI VC Trade account balances; external-wallet withdrawals are not possible. Public-chain distribution is conditional on legal/tax treatment being clarified and supervisory confirmation. The release explicitly describes a preliminary account-limited launch, not public-chain circulation.

SBI VC Trade's official 2026-11-02 release reports JPYSC Lending (貸コイン) balance above ¥10B and JPYSC handling balance above ¥30B. The lending program has customers lend JPYSC to SBI VC Trade for a fee; it is not evidence of ¥10B in loans made to outside borrowers. Footnote 1 defines handling balance as the sum of the on-chain balance and lending balance. The June 24 launch release said external-wallet transfers were disabled and public-chain circulation was conditional on legal/tax treatment and supervisory confirmation; no separate public-chain go-live notice was found in this run. The term on-chain in the Nov2 balance definition is therefore unresolved and must not be treated as proof of public-chain circulation.

SBI Shinsei Trust Bank and SBI VC Trade's official 2026-09-07 release says ¥1B of JPYSC trust backing began being invested in short-term Japanese government bonds under amended Japanese rules; issued balance was approximately ¥20.1B and customer JPYSC Lending applications approximately ¥6.9B, with combined issued-plus-lending balance around ¥27B. These are issuer backing and customer lending balances, not XRP collateral.

SBI Holdings and Startale joined Open Standard on 2026-10-16; the announcement describes more than 140 participating firms including Coinbase, Mastercard, Stripe, Visa and BlackRock. SBI and Startale said they would consider a proof-of-concept for interoperability between JPYSC and Open USD (OUSD), conditional on OUSD's onchain publication. The release explicitly says this does not mean a new service or production settlement has started. Shared consortium membership is not a bilateral SBI-Coinbase XRP partnership.

SBI Holdings and Startale Group signed a basic agreement with BlackRock Financial Management and BlackRock Japan on 2026-10-27 to explore technical infrastructure, business/distribution and regulatory/market coordination for a tokenized MMF ecosystem connected to JPYSC. It is a basic agreement to explore, not a live tokenized MMF/JPYSC integration.

SBI Holdings and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group announced a capital and business alliance on 2026-10-30 to jointly consider new financial services using stablecoins and related digital assets. The announcement is a strategic exploration; no specific live XRP settlement or production service was identified.

Ripple and Coinbase announced on 2026-10-28 that RLUSD is available across Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and retail on XRPL, Base and Ethereum. Coinbase Global Exchange collateral availability was described as future at launch, not live. This is a direct RLUSD distribution relationship, not proof of XRP purchases or XRP collateral balances.

BNY announced support for eligible institutional-client custody of XRP and RLUSD and exploration of tokenized trade-finance use cases with Ripple and C2FO. No XRP or RLUSD custody balances, customer counts or transaction volumes were disclosed.

Standard Chartered launched RLUSD custody on XRPL; the separate LMAX collateral integration was described as planned, not completed. Custody capability is not evidence of actual RLUSD balances, XRP collateral utilization or payment settlement.

counter_hypotheses: RLUSD issuer-reported supply growth does not imply XRP demand; the cross-chain dashboard shows Ethereum as the majority chain and XRPL net supply contraction over its displayed 24-hour window.
SBI's RLUSD relationship is real but does not establish XRPL usage; the official SBI release is chain-silent and secondary launch reporting says Ethereum-only.
JPYSC's ¥30B handling figure is not public-chain float or XRP collateral; it includes customer lending balance and an unresolved on-chain balance definition.
USDC and RLUSD distribution economics are sensitive to reserve yields, platform balances and contractual revenue-sharing; they are not direct measures of XRP purchases.
Stablecoin onchain transaction volume is gross transfer volume, not unique users, commercial settlement value or XRP spot demand.
